meta.claims_no_flight: Genetic/fin-proportion evidence (Daane 2021) concerns fin SIZE/PROPORTION, not flight capability. No flight is demonstrated by any molecular evidence here.
meta.no_domain_impossibility: Absences are bounded, dated searches, never universal impossibility. Evidence contest is first-class.
meta.framing: Measured ranges here are PROVENANCE-SCOPED EMPIRICAL ENVELOPES of a named sample, NOT feasibility laws and NOT a binary plausibility verdict. A design outside an envelope raises an engineering question and must state a mechanism; it is not thereby 'impossible'. Organism-context transfers (e.g. zebrafish functional results -> exocoetid/halfbeak) are labelled and UNESTABLISHED. Goal is real engineering (what to measure/build next, per curated_questions), not a pass/fail gate.
meta.ar_reconciliation: Fish 1990 p.394: AR defined generically as wing span squared / wing area (Lighthill 1977; Norberg 1985). p.395: the range 3.0-16.9 is measured on INDIVIDUAL PECTORAL FINS (max in Exocoetus; Fig 3 shows no significant AR-mass correlation); Table III lists Exocoetus to 19.9. Wing area for WL is pectoral+pelvic+intervening body (p.~? Methods). Applying the pectoral-fin AR bound to a candidate whole-wing b^2/S is a FLAGGED MODELLING CHOICE (guilds 'correspondence'), not the same quantity - the denominators differ. Source re-read from the Fish 1990 PDF (pdftotext) this session + guilds primary re-read; not imported memory.
meta.update_note_2: 2026-10-31: Daane upgraded to full-text (NOAA PDF); added Saro-Cortes 2022 (robotic) + corrected Park & Choi 2010 provenance; C4 qualified (configuration-dependent, trades with lift; Oxyporhamphus survives).

flying_fish.note: Daane 2021: lat4a (L-type amino-acid transporter) x kcnh2a (K+ channel) regulate paired-fin PROPORTION; phylogenomic signatures across 35 species. No flight. Functional test in zebrafish; exocoetid side is association.
No exocoetid macromolecular data bearing on fin enlargement.
Bioelectric Vmem / K+ flux in zebrafish fin cells (kcnh2a, kcnk5b). Candidate mechanism; no exocoetid measurement.
Zebrafish fin-bud: Vmem + calcineurin set fin size (Daane 2018, Stewart 2021, Jiang 2024). Exocoetid cell data absent.
Mechanoregulated anisotropic-growth MODEL CLASS transfers (jaw-joint). Exocoetid fin-ray material/parameters absent; jaw-joint cartilage params do NOT transfer.

Fin/wing geometry: C3 fin-length ratio executable; C4 CG stability qualitative (witness Oxyporhamphus, no numeric CG retrieved in sources read). C4 stability is configuration-dependent and trades against lift (Saro-Cortes 2022 robotic model; Park & Choi 2010 physical model); Oxyporhamphus refutation survives.
Launch/glide attitude control ('rising and turning') not modelled or measured for exocoetids.
Wing loading, AR, launch speed, size envelope: C1,C2,C5,C6b executable arithmetic (Fish 1990, Park & Choi 2010, FishBase).
Fin allometry measured across clade (Daane Fig 1B; exact values in figures). Juveniles <0.05 m do not glide (Fish 1990). Exocoetid developmental series absent.
Schooling exists but is not part of the fin-engineering design problem; not occupied here.

C6a: design placeable on time-calibrated tree (Fish Tree of Life). Ancestor RECONSTRUCTED as nested-within-halfbeaks (Lovejoy 2004) - hypothesis, not proven reachable. Predator-escape pressure asserted 167 yr, never quantified (claim, not constraint).

sources.note: Phylogenomics 35 species; >300,000 loci; 48/17,937 genes convergent rate-shift; lat4a x kcnh2a interaction PHENOCOPIES flying-fish fin PROPORTION in zebrafish. Bioelectric + amino-acid transport. NO FLIGHT demonstrated by the genetics; exocoetid side is association, functional test is zebrafish. ORGANISM-CONTEXT TRANSFER (labelled, UNESTABLISHED): the functional phenocopy is in ZEBRAFISH; the flying-fish side is phylogenomic association. This does NOT establish that enlarging a halfbeak's or an exocoetid's paired fins is experimentally grounded - that is a cross-organism transfer hypothesis, not a result. Full text adds: the 'flying halfbeaks' Euleptorhamphus and Oxyporhamphus show pectoral allometry INTERMEDIATE between halfbeaks and flying fishes (living intermediates on the fin-size axis).
